title: Where Should Raw Meat Be Stored in the Refrigerator?

seo.title: Where Should Raw Meat Be Stored in the Refrigerator?
seo.meta_description: Raw meat, poultry, and seafood should be kept cold and in containers or wrapping that prevent juices from contaminating other foods.
seo.search_intent: Make a practical, safe decision about “Where Should Raw Meat Be Stored in the Refrigerator,” recognize important limits, and know when to change approach or get help.

excerpt: Raw meat, poultry, and seafood should be kept cold and in containers or wrapping that prevent juices from contaminating other foods. content_html:
Raw meat, poultry, and seafood should be kept cold and in containers or wrapping that prevent juices from contaminating other foods. In a refrigerator maintained at 40°F (4°C) or below, properly chilled areas can be safe; keeping contained raw packages on a lower shelf adds practical protection against drips onto ready-to-eat food.

Keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below

Keep it at 40°F (4°C) or below. Use an appliance thermometer to verify actual temperature rather than relying only on the dial number. Do not pack the refrigerator so tightly that air circulation is blocked, because that can create warmer areas.

Always contain raw meat juices

Store packages in a tray, sealed container, or clean bag that can catch leaks. The goal is to keep raw juices from reaching produce, leftovers, or foods that will not be cooked again.

A lower shelf reduces risk if packaging fails

Keeping the raw-meat container below ready-to-eat foods makes gravity work in your favor if a leak occurs. That does not mean placing it directly on a dirty surface: still use secondary containment and clean any spill promptly.

Follow the refrigerated storage time for each product

Refrigerator placement does not extend shelf life indefinitely. Cook or freeze within the safe interval for the type of meat and purchase date; if food spent too long at an unsafe temperature, chilling it again does not reset the clock.

faq.question: What temperature should a refrigerator maintain?
faq.answer: Keep it at 40°F (4°C) or below. Use an appliance thermometer to verify actual temperature rather than relying only on the dial number. Do not pack the refrigerator so tightly that air circulation is blocked, because that can create warmer areas.

faq.question: Why should raw meat have secondary containment?
faq.answer: Store packages in a tray, sealed container, or clean bag that can catch leaks. The goal is to keep raw juices from reaching produce, leftovers, or foods that will not be cooked again.

faq.question: Does raw meat always have to be on the bottom shelf?
faq.answer: Keeping the raw-meat container below ready-to-eat foods makes gravity work in your favor if a leak occurs. That does not mean placing it directly on a dirty surface: still use secondary containment and clean any spill promptly.
